summary: Small tools that need nothing but a Loom session: a stepping journey and a session report.

tools.name: steps
tools.summary: Walk a few named steps, optionally wait at a release gate, and write a report file.
tools.description: A tool with no application behind it, for learning the session and for testing it: it names each step it takes, can hold at a gate until a file appears (so a run can be left pending while no client is attached), can work in a loop that COOPERATES with a cancellation instead of waiting at anything, can fail on purpose at a named step (so failure and cleanup can be seen), and writes report.txt listing what it did.

inputs.name: hold
inputs.help: hold after the first step until <run>/release/<hold> exists; empty: never hold

inputs.name: cooperate
inputs.help: work in a loop for up to this many seconds, checking ctx.cancel_requested each turn and returning early when it is true; 0: never (see steps.py)

inputs.name: fail_at
inputs.help: fail on purpose at this step; 0: never

inputs.name: crash_at
inputs.help: raise an error (a tool bug) at this step; 0: never

outputs.name: report.txt
outputs.help: one line per step, then the message

requires: nothing beyond a session with the loom-runs manager
tools.example: loom-session run <dir> basics/steps --name first --input count=2 --input hold=go
tools.recovery: fail_at ends the run 'failed' and crash_at ends it 'error'; both run the tool's cleanup, which writes cleanup.txt. A held run waits until its gate file exists or it is cancelled. A run given `cooperate` never waits at anything, so a cancellation reaches it only through ctx.cancel_requested; it returns its own verdict, which is why such a run is `passed` with cancel_requested set rather than `cancelled`.

tools.name: session-report
tools.summary: Ask the session's door what this session is -- lifetime, connections, links -- and write it down.
tools.description: Records what it is about to ask (request.txt), asks the door (loom.session.Describe), checks that the answer is about this run's own lifetime and lists this run's own session as an admitted run, and writes the answer (session.json). Asking another office is refused by the bus: this tool is granted the door, and nothing else.

inputs.name: office
inputs.help: the office to ask; anything but loom.session is refused, which is how a refusal after partial work looks

outputs.name: session.json
outputs.help: the door's description of this session

requires: a session host (loom-host --serve); its run manager allowed to pass on the rule below
tools.recovery: A dispatch refusal (CapabilityDenied) means the run's session may not ask that office: its grant names loom.session only. If loom.session itself is refused, the run manager was not allowed to pass the rule on: authority allow runs loom.session.Describe v1 -> role loom.session.
